jobs.title: Customer Assistant - Ballincollig Express
jobs.desc:
About the role
We pride ourselves on offering customers the biggest range of products around. And that's not just food, but everything from clothes and kettles to financial services.
But did you know we offer the biggest job opportunities too? With stores across the UK and Ireland, and a variety of roles, we are always looking for people who are as passionate about helping customers as we are.
Our Every Little Helps approach doesn't just apply to our customers. It's at the very heart of everything we do at work - and it's what makes us different. We believe in treating each other with respect, and everyone having the opportunity to get on. That's what makes Tesco such a great place to work.
Should you be successful in your application, your offer will be subject to and conditional upon you providing your bank account details before your agreed start date.
You will be responsible for
Always put the customer first and consider them in everything you do.
Get to know your customers and serve them with pride.
Help to ensure products and services are available for customers at all times.
Handle all products with care to maintain quality and ensure they reach the customer in the best condition.
Keep the shop floor and back areas clean and tidy at all times.
Using the training you receive, follow department routines and processes.
Follow all company policies and adhere to Health and Safety routines.
Whilst you will have a core role, you may be asked to support your colleagues by helping in other departments.
You will need
Able to give great, natural customer service by proactively smiling, greeting, acknowledging and helping customers.
Works hard for customers, your team and your department.
You are able to prioritise to ensure anything you do is right for our customers.
Adaptable and resilient to meet the ever changing demands of our business.
You must be able to follow instructions either verbal or written.
You are reliable and a good timekeeper.
You must be smart and tidy at all times.
Whats in it for you?
We offer excellent benefits that help make Tesco a great place to work. These include but aren't limited to:
Competitive Salary
Bonus Scheme*
Our Virtual GP service provides free and confidential access to an online GP through video GP consultations, and online prescription service for colleagues. The service is also available to families of colleagues who live at the same address for a reduced cost.
24/7 access to our Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) for you and family members for in the moment emotional support along with free access to a range of wellbeing services supporting you under our new Wellbeing First approach of Body, Mind and Life.
Colleague Clubcard offering 10% discount across stores and online, with 15% discount weekends once a month (Friday to Sunday), and 20% off twice a year. There is also 20% off F&F clothing, all year long, these various discounts can be extended to a family member with a 2nd Clubcard available.*
Life Assurance
Pension Plan*
Save As You Earn Scheme*
Paid Family Leave
Bike to Work
Long Service Awards
Commuter Scheme
*Entry requirements and rules of the scheme apply
About Us
Our vision at Tesco is to become every customer's favourite way to shop, whether they are at home or out on the move. Our core purpose is "Serving our customers, communities and planet a little better every day". Serving means more than a transactional relationship with our customers. It means acting as a responsible and sustainable business for all stakeholders, for the communities we are part of, and for the planet. Through initiatives like the Tesco Community Fund, our association with Children's Health Foundation, our partnership with FoodCloud and our Stronger Starts programme, we have supported over 21,000 community groups, raised over €7.5 million for medical equipment, and provided almost 15 million meals nationwide, to those living in food insecurity.
Tesco has operated in the Irish retail market since 1997, and with 190+ stores nationwide, we employ over 13,000 people in cities and towns around Ireland, supporting almost 45,000 jobs directly and indirectly. We partner with over 500 Irish suppliers - of which almost three-quarters are small and medium enterprises - which in turn supports almost 13,000 farming families around Ireland. Tesco is the single largest buyer of Irish food and drink in the world, buying €1.6 Billion a year; more than any other single country in the European Union, more than even the USA which you perceive as a massive buyer of Irish food.
We work closely with suppliers across Ireland who are dedicated to making the best products for our customers and this is reflected in the numerous awards our products have won over the years including Blás Na hÉireann, World Steak Challenge and Great Taste Awards.
We are proud to have an inclusive culture at Tesco where everyone truly feels able to be themselves. It is embedded in our values: we treat people how they want to be treated. At Tesco, we not only celebrate diversity, but recognise the value and opportunity it brings. We always want our colleagues to feel they can be themselves at work and we are committed to helping them be at their best.
We know life looks a little different for each of us. That's why at Tesco, we always welcome chats about flexible working. Some people are at the start of their careers, some want the freedom to do the things they love. Others are going through life-changing moments like becoming a carer, nearing retirement, adapting to parenthood, or something else. So, talk to us throughout your application about how we can support.
Tesco is committed to celebrating diversity and everyone is welcome at Tesco. We're committed to providing a fully inclusive recruitment process, allowing candidates the opportunity to thrive and inform us of any reasonable adjustments they may require. For further information on the accessibility support we can offer, please click http://roi.tesco-careers.com/accessibility/
How can I let Tesco know I need additional support?
Please let us know you need additional support by emailing tescoireland.recruitment@tesco.ie
This will allow us to understand more about you and how we can best support you through the recruitment process.

jobs.title: Quality Engineer
jobs.desc:
Quality Engineer
Location: Cork, Ireland
Duration: 12 month Contract
Hours: 39
Imagine your next project utilising Quality Engineering tools and principles across the complete product lifecycle to support medical devices and diagnostics that impact patients worldwide.
Global Services, LLC., represents more than 60 manufacturing sites and 26,000 employees who plan, source, manufacture and deliver high-quality and cost-effective medical products to our customers around the globe each day. Work of the MD&D Supply Chain supports a multitude of product platforms, new products and delivery systems that are used in a wide range of procedures throughout the healthcare industry, including interventional cardiology, electrophysiology, minimally invasive surgery, hospital sterilization, clinical laboratory testing, diabetes management, joint replacement surgery and vision care.
The Quality Engineer conducts assignments encompassing complete projects or portions of major projects and determines methods and techniques to be used or adapts standard methods to meet variations. The Quality Engineer utilises Quality Engineering tools and practices for the effective and efficient development, transfer, and maintenance of products/processes throughout the product lifecycle and Quality Engineering principles and problem-solving skills to improve and maintain products/processes that are aligned with the overall Quality and Business vision. They utilise appropriate risk management to prevent unanticipated failure modes and improve capability of processes.
This position acts in accordance with all applicable federal, state and local laws/regulations and Corporate Johnson & Johnson procedures and guidelines. The role reports to the Quality Engineering Leader and partners with R&D and other cross-functional partners to ensure the proper application of design controls, NPI design transfer risk management and the investigation/correction of design failures/challenges. Additionally, this position partners with Global Supply Chain, finished goods and material suppliers to ensure appropriate application of process validation, process control, and risk management; and the investigation/correction of process failures when needed.
roles and responsibilities
Support Continuous Improvement, Quality Assurance and Performance through Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, PDCA.
Collect data and execute/conduct various analytical/statistical analyses and interpretation as part of process improvements and day-to-day support.
Review the effectiveness of continuous improvement tools and techniques; conduct benchmarking to develop more effective methods for improving quality.
Implement and review effectiveness of Non-Conformance Reporting and CAPA.
Analyse/review current product and processes are in compliance to ISO 13485, QSR etc., and champion compliance to global regulations such as FDA, MDR, support internal and external audits.
Conduct periodic line audits for compliance to production controls and review audit findings for NonConformance and CAPA.
Support activities in material review board, material identification, segregation, and defect classification.
Initiate escalation for non-conformance, implement immediate corrective actions and conduct investigation, root cause analysis and bounding of non-conformance as per established process.
Develop, interpret, and implement appropriate process monitoring and control methods consistent with the level of process/product risk.
Develop, interpret, and implement standard and non-standard sampling plans.
Assess effectiveness of measurement tools, destructive tests, non-destructive tests, measurement system analysis.
Assess and interpret common versus special cause variation in manufacturing processing and determine adequacy of current process limits.
Conduct failure modes cause analysis for products and processes.
Document, justify, review, or analyse whether a proposed change to a process will not enhance the risk level in some way beyond capability of current controls or whether change will result in potential noncompliance to a required standard.
Assess the need for risk mitigation techniques given product classification, potential defect types, defect frequency, severity, patient risk, process capability, process controls, etc.
Determine effectiveness of these techniques on previously implemented improvements.
Conduct, review, and approve IQ, OQ/PQ and CSV for manufacturing and test equipment.
Establishes suitable measurement systems through the principles of MSA for the collection and analysis of unbiased, reliable, and consistent data e.g., Gauge Repeatability and Reproducibility.
Analyzes and reviews sources of variation in measurement systems, with a view to control of variation.
Ensures effective quality strategies are created for the validation of test methods, process, and design.
how to succeed
A minimum of a bachelor’s degree, preferably in Engineering or related technical field.
2-4 years’ experience in a related position.
Experience working in both an FDA and European regulatory environment is preferred
Requires relevant experience working in manufacturing/operations.
Experience with a proven track record of implementing appropriate risk mitigation.
Technical training and experience using Statistics, Lean and Six Sigma Methodologies is preferred, i.e., Measurement System Analysis, SPC, DOEs, Reliability, etc.
Strong knowledge of statistical software packages is preferred and ability to preview, graph and analyze data and be able to present data that facilitates/drives decision making.
Ability to perform "hands on" troubleshooting and problem solving is preferred, to think on their feet and providing sound judgment is highly desired.
Good technical understanding of manufacturing equipment and processes is required.
Understanding of the NPI (New Product Introduction) process and Process Validation expertise is preferred.
A thorough understanding of GMP/ISO regulations for validation and product/process Risk Management (FDA and ISO standards) is preferred.
benefits
This role offers a very competitive hourly rate. This contract will run for 12 months

Registered Nurse (Disability& Epilepsy Support) – Cork
Dovida Ireland
is seeking an experienced and compassionate
NMBI Registered Nurse
to support a young adult with complex epilepsy and intellectual disabilities in the Cork area. This is an opportunity to make a meaningful difference while working as part of a dedicated multidisciplinary support team. The role combines nursing care with person-centred support to enable the individual to live safely and participate in their community. The position involves 10 hours per week, with shifts currently scheduled for Fridays and Saturdays.
Position Details
10 hours per week
Friday: 5 hours
Saturday: 5 hours
Working alongside an experienced caregivers
Cork location

Provide safe, person-centred nursing support to a young adult with intellectual disabilities and complex epilepsy.

Support the implementation of clinical and behavioural support plans.
Work collaboratively with family members, healthcare professionals and the wider support team.

Current registration with the

Strong clinical assessment and decision-making skills.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Full driving licence and access to own transport preferred.

CPI (Crisis Prevention Intervention) Training

All mandatory Dovida training requirements

Competitive hourly rate.

Ongoing clinical support and supervision.

The opportunity to be part of an innovative and growing disability service.

jobs.title: Customer Assistant (Festive) - Mallow
jobs.desc:
About the role
Contract: Temporary
Fancy a festive in-store role? We’ve got all kinds of shifts and roles available.
Across the country, customers are counting on us to make the magic happen – and that’s why we need your help. Working in store, you’ll tackle a range of tasks, from serving customers and stocking shelves, to picking orders for home delivery. You’ll feel your impact every day, as you send customers home with a smile. Experience isn’t essential – all you need is the right attitude.
Because here, it all comes down to helping people: customers, colleagues, communities. If you’re warm and welcoming, you’ll fit right in with our caring, friendly bunch.
It all adds up to a role where you can do good, and feel good, while enjoying great flexibility. Let’s make every day a little better. Especially at Christmas.
#tescoxmas
You will be responsible for
You’ll help deliver Christmas for households across the nation.
You’ll provide support in store during the busy festive period.
You could be stocking shelves and making sure products are where they need to be.
Or, you could be serving customers and putting together orders for our Click and Collect service.
Whatever the task, you’ll take pride in making sure that customers get a brilliant experience.
You will need
Able to give great, natural customer service by proactively smiling, greeting, acknowledging and helping customers.
Works hard for customers, your team and your department.
You are able to prioritise to ensure anything you do is right for our customers.
Adaptable and resilient to meet the ever changing demands of our business.
You must be able to follow instructions either verbal or written.
You are reliable and a good timekeeper.
You must be smart and tidy at all times.
Whats in it for you?
We offer excellent benefits that help make Tesco a great place to work. These include but aren’t limited to:
Competitive Salary
Bonus Scheme*
Colleague Clubcard offering 10% discount across stores and online, with 15% discount weekends once a month (Friday to Sunday), and 20% off twice a year. There is also 20% off F&F clothing, all year long, these various discounts can be extended to a family member with a 2
nd
Clubcard available.
Life Assurance
Pension Plan*
Save As You Earn Scheme*
Paid Family Leave
Bike to Work
Long Service Awards
Commuter Scheme
Wellbeing Initiatives
*Entry requirements and rules of the scheme apply
About Us
Our vision at Tesco is to become every customer’s favourite way to shop, whether they are at home or out on the move.  Our core purpose is “Serving our customers, communities and planet a little better every day”.  Serving means more than a transactional relationship with our customers.  It means acting as a responsible and sustainable business for all stakeholders, for the communities we are part of, and for the planet. Through initiatives like the Tesco Community Fund, our association with Children’s Health Foundation, our partnership with FoodCloud and our Stronger Starts programme, we have supported over 21,000 community groups, raised over €7.5 million for medical equipment, and provided almost 15 million meals nationwide, to those living in food insecurity.
Tesco has operated in the Irish retail market since 1997, and with 170 stores nationwide, we employ over 13,000 people in cities and towns around Ireland, supporting almost 45,000 jobs directly and indirectly. We partner with over 500 Irish suppliers - of which almost three-quarters are small and medium enterprises - which in turn supports almost 13,000 farming families around Ireland. Tesco is the single largest buyer of Irish food and drink in the world, buying €1.6 Billion a year; more than any other single country in the European Union, more than even the USA which you perceive as a massive buyer of Irish food.
We work closely with suppliers across Ireland who are dedicated to making the best products for our customers and this is reflected in the numerous awards our products have won over the years including Blás Na hÉireann, World Steak Challenge and Great Taste Awards.
We are proud to have an inclusive culture at Tesco where everyone truly feels able to be themselves. It is embedded in our values: we treat people how they want to be treated.   At Tesco, we not only celebrate diversity, but recognise the value and opportunity it brings.  We always want our colleagues to feel they can be themselves at work and we are committed to helping them be at their best.
We know life looks a little different for each of us. That’s why at Tesco, we always welcome chats about flexible working. Some people are at the start of their careers, some want the freedom to do the things they love. Others are going through life-changing moments like becoming a carer, nearing retirement, adapting to parenthood, or something else. So, talk to us throughout your application about how we can support.
Tesco is committed to celebrating diversity and everyone is welcome at Tesco. We're committed to providing a fully inclusive recruitment process, allowing candidates the opportunity to thrive and inform us of any reasonable adjustments they may require. For further information on the accessibility support we can offer, please click http://roi.tesco-careers.com/accessibility/
How can I let Tesco know I need additional support?
Please let us know you need additional support by emailing
tescoireland.recruitment@tesco.ie
This will allow us to understand more about you and how we can best support you through the recruitment process.

jobs.title: Production Planner
jobs.desc:
About Munters
Munters is a global leader in climate solutions for mission-critical processes. Through innovative and energy-efficient technologies, we enable customers across industries to control humidity, temperature, and energy use efficiently. Together, we support our customers in optimizing performance while contributing to a healthier planet.
With more than 70 years of experience, Munters serves industries such as Data Centers, Battery production, Food, Pharma, and Manufacturing worldwide. We combine innovation, sustainability, and engineering expertise to create solutions that make a real difference for both our customers and the environment.
At Munters, you will be part of a collaborative and international organization where continuous improvement, knowledge sharing, and personal growth are encouraged. Come as you are and be part of our journey.
Main Areas Of Responsibilities
Production Planning and Scheduling
Develop and maintain production schedules that align with customer demand, sales forecasts, and manufacturing capacity. This involves analysing customer orders, sales projections, and manufacturing capabilities to create detailed production plans that outline the sequence and timing of production activities.
Analyse production requirements, material availability, and labour resources to optimize production planning. This involves assessing the materials, components, and labour needed for each product, identifying potential constraints, and adjusting the production schedule to ensure efficient resource utilization and timely order fulfilment.
Schedule production activities to ensure smooth flow of materials, efficient resource utilization, and timely completion of orders. This involves breaking down production processes into individual tasks, assigning tasks to specific workstations or teams, and coordinating the movement of materials and components throughout the production process.
Production Process Optimization
Analyse production processes to identify areas for improvement, potential bottlenecks, and waste reduction opportunities. This involves conducting detailed process reviews, collecting data on process performance, and identifying areas where efficiency can be enhanced, lead times can be reduced, and costs can be minimized.
Implement process improvements to enhance efficiency, reduce lead times, and minimize production costs. This involves developing and implementing process changes, such as streamlining workflows, introducing new technologies, or adopting lean manufacturing principles, to achieve operational excellence.
Collaborate with engineering and operations teams to optimize production processes and ensure adherence to quality standards. This involves working closely with engineering teams to design and implement process improvements, and collaborating with operations teams to ensure that new processes are effectively implemented and monitored for adherence to quality standards.
You will also be expected to carry out any additional duties that may be assigned to you by the company from time to time.

jobs.title: Solutions Engineer, EMEA
jobs.desc:
About Nooks.ai
Nooks is an applied AI lab building the Agent Workspace for GTM. We design AI agents that operate across the full sales action set, from
account strategy
to
prospect research
and
outreach
. Building 0→1 has never been easier, but selling at the speed of the market remains the last frontier for AI. Our mission is to 10x every seller by automating the busywork so they can focus on what humans do best: closing deals.
Today, over 1,500 customers run on Nooks, including Notion, HubSpot, Cursor, and Rippling. We’ve raised $70M+ from top VCs like Kleiner Perkins, which made its first sales-tech investment in over a decade with us. Since then, we’ve tripled ARR each year for 3 years running and grown a high-caliber team turning the art of sales into a scalable science.
Title:
Founding Solutions Engineer (EMEA)
Location:
Primary: Dublin; secondary: Remote, UK or Ireland
About The Role
Nooks is the Agent Workspace for Sales, where reps and AI agents don’t just execute tasks, they decide next moves, with intelligence that compounds over time. We’re growing fast (4x YoY since Series B), our customers spend 4+ hours a day inside Nooks, and the SE function is one of the highest-leverage bets in the business: SE-supported deals close at nearly 6x the rate of unsupported ones.
As our
first Solutions Engineer in EMEA
, you’ll partner with the founding EMEA GTM team to build the territory and establish how we win technically in the region. You’ll own technical discovery, demos, and trial strategy while building the processes, tools, and customer experiences that make the motion repeatable.
You’ll have an established global SE foundation to build on, alongside substantial ownership of what needs to work differently in EMEA. That means adapting our playbook to regional buying processes, creating new approaches where needed, and turning early customer learning into a stronger sales motion.
We’re looking for someone who enjoys both winning deals and building the systems behind them. If you’re a seller who thinks like an engineer, or an engineer who’s found their competitive edge in the deal, this is built for you.
What You'll Do
Own the technical win across EMEA: Lead the full technical sales lifecycle across concurrent opportunities, from discovery and demo through trial and close, with a clear mandate to drive each to a decision.
Build the territory with the founding EMEA GTM team: Partner with AEs and regional leadership on account strategy, customer engagement, and the technical approach needed to create and win early opportunities.
Create an EMEA-specific SE motion: Adapt and build discovery frameworks, demo narratives, trial plans, success criteria, and handoffs that reflect regional customer needs and buying processes.
Connect technical discovery to business outcomes: Get underneath feature requests to uncover real business pain, then build a solution narrative tied to executive priorities and measurable value.
Lead prospect trials: Serve as the primary technical contact, establish clear evaluation plans, monitor trial health, flag risks early, and intervene before issues threaten the deal.
Navigate complex evaluations: Coordinate with internal experts on integrations, security, data handling, and procurement requirements, keeping customers aligned on a credible path forward.
Build the regional operating foundation: Create reusable assets, document what works, and introduce automation that helps a small team cover more opportunities effectively.
Connect the EMEA field to Product: Translate recurring customer needs, competitive insights, and trial patterns into actionable feedback for Product and the global SE team.
Help shape future SE growth in EMEA: Codify the regional playbook and contribute to onboarding and developing future teammates as the business grows.
What You Bring
Prior experience in a quota-carrying or technical sales role, such as AE, SE, or hybrid, with ownership of the pre-sale cycle.
Experience supporting EMEA customers and navigating regional buying processes, stakeholder dynamics, and technical evaluations.
A builder’s mindset: you can create a process, test it in live deals, and improve it without waiting for a complete playbook.
A sales-first instinct: you treat trials like pipeline, care deeply about win rates, and build urgency around real customer priorities.
The ability to engage senior stakeholders, including CROs, CTOs, and VPs of Sales, and lead discovery or a business review independently.
Technical curiosity and sound reasoning: you understand how systems connect, investigate unfamiliar requirements, and close knowledge gaps independently.
Strong discovery skills: you ask “why is that a requirement?” before answering it and develop a point of view before prescribing a solution.
The judgment to prioritize across active deals and foundational work, knowing when to solve something yourself and when to involve global partners.
A bias toward action and comfort owning ambiguous, undocumented work as the first SE in a new region.
Early regional expansion or founding-team experience is a strong plus, as is familiarity with MEDDIC, MEDDPICC, or an equivalent enterprise sales methodology.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
Nooks is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workforce. We believe in providing equal employment opportunities to all individuals regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.
Nooks does not discriminate in hiring, promotion, compensation, or any other employment practices, and we are committed to ensuring a workplace that is free from discrimination, harassment, and retaliation. We encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply and join our team.

Looking to earn a little extra this festive season? What better way to do it than in an iconic store, surrounded by the products you love and with a 25% discount for the duration of your contract with us!
We’re looking for warm, friendly people who love fashion and retail to deliver unforgettable customer experiences in our stores this festive season!

jobs.title: Renewal Specialist
jobs.desc:
Job Description
We Are Omnissa!
Omnissa is the first AI-driven digital work platform, built to support flexible, secure, work-from-anywhere experiences. We integrate industry-leading solutions—including Unified Endpoint Management, Virtual Apps and Desktops, Digital Employee Experience, and Security & Compliance—into a seamless, autonomous workspace that adapts to how people work. Our platform boosts employee engagement while optimizing IT operations, security, and cost.

What is the opportunity?
We are seeking Renewals Specialist - Fluent German to support our Corporate Accounts business. In this role, you will manage a high volume of renewals in a more transactional model, ensuring contracts are renewed efficiently and accurately. The Corporate Renewals team differs from our Premier and Strategic teams, which focus heavily on account management and long-term customer engagement due to the size and complexity of their renewals.
The Corporate team is designed to be transactional, volume-driven, and fast-paced, requiring strong organizational skills and a disciplined approach to pipeline management. This role is also an excellent fit for early-career professionals. Historically, we’ve seen great success hiring recent graduates, individuals transitioning from retail sales, or those looking to move into SaaS and technology sales. The key is drive and ambition—many of our team members have leveraged this opportunity as a stepping stone into field sales or account management roles.
Key Responsibilities:
Renewal Pipeline Management
• Manage the end-to-end renewal process for a high volume of assigned customer accounts.
• Proactively engage with customers 90–120 days in advance to confirm contract terms and secure renewals.
• Ensure all renewal communications (notifications, reminders, confirmations) are accurate and timely.
Customer Engagement
• Serve as the first point of contact for renewal discussions.
• Help customers recognize the ongoing value of Omnissa’s solutions.
• Escalate customer concerns to the appropriate internal teams when needed.
Retention & Growth
• Identify at-risk accounts and flag them for follow-up by Customer Success or Sales.
• Spot upsell or cross-sell opportunities where appropriate and route to Account Executives.
• Consistently deliver high retention rates by executing a disciplined, transactional renewal process.
Process & Reporting
• Maintain detailed records of all renewal activities in Salesforce.
• Track and report on renewal rates, churn risks, and upsell opportunities.
• Provide insights to improve renewal operations and customer touchpoints.
What will you bring to Omnissa?
• 0-2 years of experience in customer-facing or sales-related roles (SaaS, subscription-based, retail sales, or similar).
• Strong drive and motivation to build a career in technology sales.
• Ability to thrive in a high-volume, transactional sales environment.
• Excellent communication and organizational skills.
• Customer-first mindset with a focus on efficiency and accuracy.
• Familiarity with CRM systems (Salesforce preferred).
• Fluent German
Location:
Cork, Ireland
Location Type:
Hybrid - 3 days per week in office
Omnissa is committed to building a workforce that reflects the communities we serve across the globe. We believe this brings unique perspectives, experiences, and ideas, which are essential for driving innovation and achieving business success. We hire based on merit and provide equal opportunity for all.

Stepping Ahead Clinic provides comprehensive assessments and therapeutic supports for children and young people from infancy through adolescence in well-equipped therapy centers located in Blackpool and Carrigaline. jobs.title: Sr. Analyst, Payroll AMR
jobs.desc:
Logitech is the Sweet Spot for people who want their actions to have a positive global impact while having the flexibility to do it in their own way.
Global Payroll Senior Analyst
Position Summary:
Department: Controllership Finance – Global Payroll Team
Location: Cork, Ireland - On site 2 days a week
Contract Type: Full Time / Permanent
Region Coverage: AMR
About the Role:
As an integral member of Logitech Finance, you will work in a fast-paced, dynamic Global Payroll team processing payrolls across the Americas region — covering the United States, Canada, and Latin America. You will play a key role in ensuring accurate, compliant, and timely payroll delivery, while helping to drive continuous improvement across our payroll operations.
Your Contribution:
Be Yourself. Be Open. Stay Hungry and Humble. Collaborate. Challenge. Decide and Do.
In this role you will:
Ensure the accurate and timely processing of Logitech’s end-to-end payroll for the AMR region (USA, Canada, and LATAM).
Collaborate with payroll partners to collect and validate all payroll inputs, including salaries, bonuses, benefits, allowances, and deductions. Conduct rigorous pre- and post-payroll reconciliations to eliminate anomalies or duplicate records before finalization.
Ensure the accurate and timely completion of payroll fiscal close procedures, including journal entries and balance sheet reconciliations. Work with the broader Finance team to identify and resolve payroll accounting exceptions.
Understand the full payroll cycle through to GL bookings and present meaningful flux analysis to stakeholders.
Stay current on and ensure strict compliance with federal, state/provincial, and local payroll regulations, tax laws, social security, and benefits requirements across all AMR jurisdictions.
Ensure compliance with payroll internal controls, maintaining robust documentation and proactively identifying and remediating any control gaps or weaknesses. Assist in facilitating internal and external audit engagements.
Partner with key stakeholders including People Services, HRIS, Compensation & Benefits, Stock Admin, and Finance to troubleshoot issues and work collaboratively to develop optimum processes and service delivery.
Drive the payroll Global Finance Transformation roadmap, focusing on eliminating manual workflows and implementing scalable, automated payroll solutions.
Collaborate with internal and external partners to drive automation and enhance service delivery.
Your Skills & Experience:
Beyond core technical payroll knowledge, we are seeking an innovative, highly data-literate payroll professional who actively identifies opportunities to leverage modern tools, AI, and emerging technologies to automate workflows and transform end-to-end payroll operations.
For consideration, you must bring the following skills, experience and behaviours to our team:
Experience: 3+ years of proven experience in a senior analyst payroll role, specifically working with Americas payroll (US required; Canada and LATAM experience is a major plus).
Education & Certification: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, or a related field—or an equivalent payroll certification.
Regulatory Compliance: Solid understanding of US/Canadian payroll taxes, statutory deductions, and labour regulations.
Hands-on experience processing payroll and running reports in Workday and/or Dayforce (Ceridian).
Spreadsheet Skills: Advanced proficiency in MS Excel and Google Sheets (must be comfortable using Pivot Tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, and managing large data sets).
Familiarity with how HRIS data flows into downstream payroll and Finance/GL systems.
Strong ability to perform pre- and post-payroll reconciliations, investigate gross-to-net variances, and flag data errors before finalization.
Experience supporting month-end close procedures, including preparing journal entries and assisting Finance/FP&A teams with cost analysis.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills to partner effectively across HR, Finance, and external vendors.
Ability to stay organized and solve problems independently in a fast-paced, global team environment.
Customer service focus with the ability and sound judgment to handle highly sensitive information.
Process improvement mindset: have a passion for reengineering payroll processes in implementing a first-class payroll service.
Strong interest in applying emerging technologies—such as AI, ML, and RPA—to re-engineer enterprise payroll workflows, eliminate manual touchpoints, and unlock value-added insights for workforce planning.
About Logitech
With a fast-moving, innovative culture and a strong balance sheet, Logitech is a world leader in products that connect people to the digital experiences they care most about. Video conferencing, remote work, content creation, and gaming are long-term secular trends driving our business — and today all of them have accelerated, making Logitech more relevant to customers than ever.
Logitech is the sweet spot for people who are passionate about products, making a mark, and having fun doing it. We're small and flexible enough for every person to take initiative — and big enough for those actions to have a global impact.
Across Logitech we empower collaboration and foster play. We help teams collaborate/learn from anywhere, without compromising on productivity or continuity so it should be no surprise that most of our jobs are open to work from home from most locations. Our hybrid work model allows some employees to work remotely while others work on-premises. Within this structure, you may have teams or departments split between working remotely and working in-house.
Logitech is an amazing place to work because it is full of authentic people who are inclusive by nature as well as by design. Being a global company, we value our diversity and celebrate all our differences. Don’t meet every single requirement? Not a problem. If you feel you are the right candidate for the opportunity, we strongly recommend that you apply. We want to meet you!
We offer comprehensive and competitive benefits packages and working environments that are designed to be flexible and help you to care for yourself and your loved ones, now and in the future. We believe that good health means more than getting medical care when you need it. Logitech supports a culture that encourages individuals to achieve good physical, financial, emotional, intellectual and social wellbeing so we all can create, achieve and enjoy more and support our families. We can’t wait to tell you more about them being that there are too many to list here and they vary based on location.

jobs.desc:
The Opportunity
THE OPPORTUNITY
This is an opportunity to join Stantec’s growing water sector team in Ireland, where you will contribute to the delivery of critical infrastructure that supports communities, protects the environment, and addresses the challenges of climate change. As a Civil Engineer, you will work on a diverse range of water and wastewater projects, from concept and feasibility through to detailed design and construction support, gaining exposure across the full project lifecycle.
You will be part of a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment, working alongside experts in engineering, environmental science, and planning to deliver integrated and sustainable solutions. The role offers the chance to build your technical expertise in areas such as network design, treatment processes, and asset management, while also developing your project management and client-facing skills
About The Role
As a Civil Engineer in Stantec’s water team, you will support the delivery of water and wastewater projects across all stages, from concept to construction. You will contribute to technical design work, including drawings, calculations, and specifications, while assisting with reports and contract documentation.
Working within a multidisciplinary team, you will collaborate with engineers, environmental specialists, and project managers, gaining broad project experience and exposure to clients and stakeholders. This role offers a strong platform to develop your technical skills and grow your career within Ireland’s water sector.
YOUR IMPACT
In this role, you will contribute to the delivery of essential water and wastewater infrastructure that supports communities, public health, and environmental protection across Ireland. Your work will help ensure reliable water services, improve network performance, and enhance resilience to climate change.
By applying sound engineering principles and attention to detail, you will support the development of practical, efficient, and sustainable design solutions. Your input will help projects meet regulatory requirements, reduce environmental impact, and deliver long-term value for clients and stakeholders.
Through collaboration with multidisciplinary teams, you will play a part in driving high-quality project outcomes, strengthening client relationships, and supporting the continued growth and reputation of Stantec in Ireland’s water sector.
About You
You are a qualified Civil Engineer with a strong technical foundation and proven experience in water network design. You bring a practical, solutions-focused mindset and are comfortable working both independently and as part of a collaborative, multidisciplinary team.
You Will Demonstrate
A minimum Level 8 degree in Engineering (or a related discipline)
Strong post-graduate experience in water network design
Solid professional and technical knowledge, with the ability to apply engineering principles effectively
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage with colleagues and clients
WHY JOIN US
We put people first: We're proud of our friendly, inclusive and collaborative environment where everyone feels valued and driven to succeed.
We are driven to achieve: Named in the top 50 companies to work by Glassdoor 2025. Recognised by Corporate Knights as one of the world's top 10 most sustainable companies 2025. =
We do what is right: Industry leading training and development as well as paid for professional subscriptions. A professional progression plan, supporting you to become chartered.
We are better together: A supportive and collaborative team environment to assist with the growth of your career.
Growth: We're on an exciting growth journey across the Ireland - we want you to be part of it!
Great Benefits: Competitive salary, enhanced pension plan, annual leave with the option to buy/sell additional days, private medical insurance, group income protection & life assurance included as standard!
About Stantec
Whether you’re starting out on your engineering career or are looking for a fresh challenge, Ryan Hanley, now part of Stantec, is a great career move.
Based in Dublin, Galway, Castlebar and Cork, we are actively recruiting for team players with experience in any of the following areas – water and wastewater treatment process and network design, integrated network management, structural design, site development, road and bridge engineering, project management and administration.
You’ll be working for a dynamic company with an excellent reputation in the industry.
Ryan Hanley, now part of Stantec, offers a great working environment amongst friendly professionals with an emphasis on teamwork. It’s a company where your ideas and opinions will be valued and your efforts recognised and rewarded.
We have been awarded the silver Investors in Diversity accreditation by the Irish Centre for Diversity for our commitment to quality, diversity and inclusion (EDI) in the workplace.

jobs.title: Kinisla Engineering Graduate 2027
jobs.desc:
Start Your Career with Kinisla!
Join the Kinisla Graduate Programme in a permanent, full-time role designed for ambitious graduates who aspire to become future senior leaders in our business. This is more than an entry-level graduate job: it is a structured two-year leadership development programme commencing September 2027. It combines formal learning, hands-on operational experience, meaningful projects, mentoring across the business. From day one, you will be challenged to build the commercial, operational and leadership capabilities needed to grow your career with Kinisla.
Assessment centres will take place during the week commencing 18 January 2027. As part of the selection process, you must be available to attend in person during that week.
Working in Engineering at Kinisla:
At Kinisla, Engineering is central to the safe, efficient and sustainable operation of our business. From milk intake through processing to final product packaging, our engineers help ensure every stage of our vertically integrated value chain performs at its best. As a graduate, you will join an experienced team and contribute to live engineering activities and projects from day one. You will work closely with Operations, Supply Chain, Food Safety & Quality, Health & Safety and other teams across the business, building practical knowledge of our production facilities, technologies, processes and products.
Your responsibilities may include:
Supporting plant operations and troubleshooting equipment issues to maintain safe and reliable production
Contributing to continuous improvement initiatives focused on energy efficiency, waste reduction and process optimisation
Collaborating with Supply Chain, Food Safety & Quality, Health & Safety and Operations to deliver cross-functional solutions
Supporting the implementation of new technologies and automation systems
Participating in capital projects, including equipment upgrades and facility enhancements
Applying lean manufacturing principles and data-led decision-making to improve performance
Building practical knowledge of dairy technologies and processes, including pasteurisation and cheese production
Developing a strong understanding of Kinisla's product portfolio and its application across retail and foodservice channels
Developing Kinisla's Future Leaders
Our Graduate Programme is designed to accelerate your development and prepare you for increasing responsibility and future leadership opportunities at Kinisla. You will benefit from:
A permanent role with structured development over two years
Off-the-job learning modules, mentoring and group projects
Hands-on responsibility and meaningful project work from day one
Opportunities to build a broad network across Kinisla
By the end of the programme, you will have built strong engineering expertise, a broad understanding of the business and the leadership foundations to progress towards more senior roles at Kinisla.
Do You Have What It Takes?
You are on track to achieve, or have recently completed, a degree with at least a 2:1 classification in Engineering or a related discipline
You can demonstrate an interest in building a career in Engineering within an FMCG and/or food manufacturing environment
You are curious, open to learning and actively seek feedback
You are a self-starter who takes ownership, prioritises effectively and adapts to changing priorities
You can influence, listen and build trust with internal and external stakeholders
You are ambitious, challenge the status quo and look for practical ways to improve the business
You are flexible to work across different sites and functions
You are eligible to work permanently in the United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland
Discover Your Future with Kinisla:
Kinisla is a vertically integrated dairy, nutritional ingredients and consumer foods business, built on more than 50 years of expertise in milk processing, dairy and nutritional ingredient technology, and product innovation.
Working in close partnership with 2,600 family farms, we produce high-quality, low-carbon-intensity milk for dairy and nutritional ingredient solutions, alongside a strong portfolio of trusted, market-leading consumer products and brands.
With manufacturing operations across Ireland, Northern Ireland and the UK, and a global customer reach, Kinisla is a trusted and forward-looking supplier of high-quality dairy products, ingredients and nutritional solutions. Our four business areas are Agribusiness, Dairy Ingredients, Nutritional Ingredients, and Consumer Foods.
Our purpose is to reimagine dairy for better food and a future worth farming for. Through expertise, innovation and responsible growth, we are helping to shape a more regenerative and climate-conscious future for our dairy.
Rooted in the South-West of Ireland, Kinisla combines deep heritage, global expertise and innovation to create exciting products, partnerships and careers. Our values are Together, Braver, and Further.

jobs.title: Health, Safety & Environmental Advisor
jobs.desc:
Req ID: 1499
Full-Time/Part-Time: Full-Time
MM is a global leader in consumer packaging. The Group provides packaging solutions for cartonboard and folding cartons with an attractive offer in kraft papers, uncoated fine papers, leaflets and labels. MM promotes sustainable development through innovative, recyclable packaging and paper products.
Our heart beats for talents - be one of them!
We are looking for an experienced
Health, Safety & Environmental Advisor
for our site in Cork
Your Role
The Site HSE Advisor will work with site management, teams and individuals in order to progress safe working practices and to develop risk assessments and safe systems of work.
You will stay up to date with relevant legislation and ensure Site MD is informed of same
You will ensure that a safe working environment is maintained at the site and that the site is working in compliance with current Health and Safety legislation, best practice and approved codes of practice (ACOP)
You will ensure that the site is working in compliance with current Environmental legislation, best practice and approved codes of practice and that the site is not conducting any practices that could have a negative impact of the environment
You will manage the risk assessment (RA) and safe working operating procedures (SWOP) process and ensuring that all Supervisors and Managers are regularly reviewing these documents in line with business standards and current legislation, guidance and ACOP
You will deliver the site Health & Safety induction programme for all new starters, contractors and visitors to site
You will manage the near miss and accident reporting processes for health and safety, and the environment and ensuring that all incidents have been fully investigated and recorded in line with business standards and current legislation, guidance and ACOP
You will ensure that the site Management team implement all corrective actions that have been established as part of an incident investigation and, within the agreed timescale
You will ensure that all health, safety and environmental documentation is current, compliant and up to date with the latest HSE format
You will identify underlying core issues/risks and engage at all site levels, both with colleagues, site technical staff and management within the site
You will maintain the site register of Interactive Safety Tours (IST) and ensure that all site Managers are conducting their tours in alignment with the agreed site schedule
You will conduct internal audits of the site
You will be a hands-on Advisor with overall accountability for developing the site safety plan and the continuous updating and monitoring of the plan
You will ensure that the site is compliant with its H&S training
You will facilitate the tri-monthly site safety committee meeting and ensure that there is a good balance of representation from the site, including the site lead and to then, create and distribute the meeting minutes
You will ensure that the site health, safety and environmental information boards are populated and up to date
You will collect and collate weekly and monthly Divisional HSE KPI data and repost externally
You will manage stocks of PPE and supplies relevant to the staff protection and well being
Your Profile
You have an undergraduate degree or equivalent qualifications (EQF Level 6)
You have 3-5 years professional experience
You have a working knowledge of formal Management systems
You are active member of IOSH or similar accredited professional body
You have the ability to communicate complex matters confidently and professionally at all levels within the organisation
You are self-disciplined and able to work to bring all projects and tasks to a suitable conclusion within agreed timescales
You possess good I.T. skills and are proficient in the use of word, excel and PowerPoint in order to create suitable professional communications
Our Offer
Join our dedicated team of passionate colleagues who like to get things done!
We offer you a workplace in a stable, international company with long-term growth path. You can also look forward to interesting tasks with a team that is collaborative, passionate, result-focused and responsible.
The following benefits complete our offer:
Onboarding including plant tour
Company events and activities
Defined contribution Pension up to 5%
Subsidised Canteen

About the Role:
The Electrical Artificer is responsible for the maintenance, repair and troubleshooting of electrical systems on our fleet of state-of-the-art ships.
You are responsible for ensuring operational readiness through maintaining essential electrical infrastructure, including power generation and distribution.

jobs.title: Kepak Operational Rotational Graduate Programme 2027 - Ireland

We are seeking to recruit for the 2027 Operational Rotational Graduate Programme at either our Kepak Longford or Kepak Cork site.
Our Operations Graduates will embark on an intensive learning journey within our business, gaining a comprehensive understanding of the entire production process from procurement to sales. This role is designed to develop future leaders in the meat industry, with a strong emphasis on learning the end-to-end process, understanding the value of each step, and mastering the operations that drive our business. The ultimate goal is for the graduate to be able to articulate the entire process, and to demonstrate this knowledge through presentations and hands-on experience.
Key Responsibilities
End-to-End Process Learning: Rotate through various operational departments, to gain hands-on experience of every role and a deep understanding of each stage of the production process
Presentation and Reporting: At the end of each rotation, present the acquired knowledge and insights to demonstrate an understanding of the operations
Operational Involvement: Actively participate on the factory floor, learning each work station and the processes involved producing our products
People Management: Develop skills in managing diverse teams, understanding the dynamics of a labour-intensive industry, and learning how to effectively communicate and lead in a multicultural environment
Continuous Improvement: Engage in key projects such as data gathering, writing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), process improvement initiatives, and customer-specific projects to contribute to the overall efficiency of operations

Other Role Information

Our Operational Graduate programme allows dynamic, motivated, hardworking, and passionate Graduates an opportunity start their career with one of the top 100 brands in the UK. The programme lasts 2 years.

jobs.title: Research Assistant- AI assisted design ICs capture BioSignals
jobs.desc:
Research Assistant- AI assisted design ICs capture BioSignals
About Tyndall
Tyndall National Institute is an international leader in semiconductors, photonics and deep-tech research and innovation. As a leading collaborative European research institute, Tyndall is a key actor and hosting partner in the delivery of the ‘Chips for Europe Initiative’ (EU Chips Act).
Tyndall is Ireland’s leading research and innovation organisation and it is the national focal point for excellence in deep-tech research, development and graduate training at the convergence of nanotechnology, microelectronics, photonics, electronics and AI. Tyndall is recognised as an international research leader in semiconductor, chip and digital technologies, particularly as applied to the fields of Information & Communications, Health & Life Sciences, Agritech & Food Security, Energy and Climate Mitigation, emerging fields such as quantum, and novel computing paradigms.
The Institute’s key objective is to see frontier research activities having a significant impact on economic development and societal challenges in Ireland, Europe and beyond. Central to Tyndall’s mission is delivering economic impact through research excellence in partnership with industry and academia. With an annual turnover of more than €50m, the Institute has a community of over 600 researchers, engineers, support staff, postgraduate students, interns and industry researchers-in-residence.
With significant committed Irish government support, Tyndall will grow to be 1,000 people by 2030, with approximately 750 researchers, including 250 PhD students. A new 17,000 m2 research building is under development adjacent to the Cork headquarters and there are developing plans to expand Tyndall’s existing Dublin research labs and to establish other research sites within Ireland.
Tyndall’s expansion is also supported by recent national and EU funding wins for significant (M€10’s) additional research equipment across a range of areas such as semiconductor processing, microscopy, quantum technologies, heterogeneous integration, ultra-high speed optical communications and RF through THz characterisation.
About the Team
The integrated circuits group at Tyndall National Institute consist of a large team of researchers in silicon chip design, at various stages of their careers; from Masters researcher through to Principal Researcher. All are creating advanced, innovative and high impact Integrated Circuit technologies, which will shape our future lives. Excellent research is being carried out in areas such as Analog Precision Circuits, RF and Millimeter-wave Communications circuits, Cryogenic CMOS and Integrated Power Systems.
About the Role
Design of a Wide-bandwidth (RF) low noise amplifier
The objective of this position is to apply AI assisted circuit design methods to design amplifiers and Analog to Digital converter blocks. The circuit blocks will be used to build a system to capture Bio electrical signals like ECG and EMG.
Key Duties & Responsibilities
The candidate is expected to be creative, self-motivated, and should help create an efficientl and friendly atmosphere within the Integrated Circuits Group and beyond to all teams at Tyndall.
Propose AI assisted design methods to Simulate, Design and Layout analogue circuits either using Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools from industry standard vendors like Cadence or custom or open source tools
With guidance from the senior Tyndall design team propose innovative circuits to meet the bio sensing application
Perform schematic design, simulation and analysis across PVT corners and relevant operating conditions
Work with guidance from experienced layout engineers to ensure effective layout implementation of analogue circuits, including matching, parasitics, shielding, grounding, isolation and other layout considerations
Prepare presentations and reports
Support project management
Participate in Education and Public Engagement activities, as required
Ensure compliance with Tyndall’s Quality Management Systems, Health and Safety standards, and other regulations
Carry out any additional duties as may reasonably be required within the general scope and level of the post
Essential Criteria
The successful candidate must have:
a MEng or equivalent experience (e.g. BEng + 2 years’ experience) in a relevant discipline such as electrical/electronic engineering, physics or related relevant discipline;
experience in designing integrated circuits in the areas of Analogue, Mixed-Signal or RF circuit design;
experience with designing and simulating integrated circuits using tools such as Cadence/Siemens-Mentor/Synoposys;
strong communication skills, as evidenced by prior experience such as working with/in industry, scientific paper writing, conference presentation and report writing
Knowledge of analogue circuits e.g. amplifiers or comparators
Knowledge of AI algorithms
Desirable Criteria
Knowledge of Integrated circuit layout
Good mathematical ability and knowledge of statistics
Experience programming with Python
What We Offer
Apart from offering a position in a highly successful and positive research environment, with a collaborative ethos full of diverse competencies to boost your career, we offer the following:
Impactful Work: Opportunities to contribute to ground-breaking research and innovation that shape Ireland’s economy and the society at large.
Continuous Learning: Strong support for formal training, further study and professional development.
Interdisciplinary Environment: Where academia, industry, and innovation intersect - supported by cutting-edge infrastructure and expert knowledge.
Blended Working: Flexibility to work remotely and on-site, where the role allows.
Comprehensive Benefits: Access to UCC pension, long-term illness benefit, life assurance, and more.
Generous Leave: Competitive annual leave entitlements.
Equity & Inclusion: Athena Swan Bronze award holder, with ongoing initiatives led by a dedicated People and Culture team to ensure equity for all.
Core Values: A culture grounded in Ambition, Collaboration, Diversity, Excellence, and Integrity.
Entrepreneurial Spirit: A proactive, innovation-driven environment that welcomes entrepreneurial and creative thinkers, including those with start-up experience.
Supportive Onboarding: Structured induction and mentoring to help new hires integrate and thrive.
Vibrant Culture: A collaborative, people-first workplace with a strong sense of community.
Terms of Employment
Contract Category: Full-Time
Contract Type: Fixed Term
The duration of the project is 7 months in the first instance, although this may be extended for an additional year pending funding and performance.
Appointment may be made on the Research Assistant Salary Scale i.e. €34,129- €44,311 per annum. Placement on appointment will be in accordance with public sector pay policy.
For further information, please contact to Dr. Daniel O' Hare.
Closing date of applications is 1pm, 16th October 2026.
Application Instructions
Please make sure to attach an up to date CV/Resume AND a brief motivation letter outlining how you meet the ‘Essential Criteria’ for this role.
Please note that Garda vetting and/or an international police clearance check may form part of the selection process.
At this time, Tyndall National Institute does not require the assistance of recruitment agencies.

About us
We are a clean energy company that develops, builds, owns and operates renewable projects across the island of Ireland, with a portfolio spanning onshore wind, solar and battery energy storage (BESS). You will work at the analytical heart of the business, supporting decisions across development, finance and operations. Expect variety, real responsibility and plenty of learning. Your work will include:
Building and maintaining models for project economics, energy production and market analysis

jobs.title: Inside Sales Representative, Mid-Market (EMEA)
jobs.desc:
Keeper is hiring a driven, Inside Sales Representative to join our high producing global sales team. Qualified candidates must permanently reside in Ireland. This is a hybrid position for those living within a commutable distance to our Cork, Ireland office, or fully remote for those living outside a commutable distance.
Keeper’s cybersecurity software is trusted by millions of people and thousands of organisations, globally. Keeper is published in 23 languages and is sold in over 150 countries. Join one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity companies and gain valuable skills while building new client relationships in this pivotal role!
About Keeper
Keeper Security is a leading cybersecurity software company that protects thousands of organizations and millions of people in more than 150 countries. Keeper delivers a powerful zero-trust and zero-knowledge solution built to meet the stringent requirements of public sector IT environments. Its flagship offering, KeeperPAM®, is an AI-enabled, cloud-native platform that protects users, devices and critical infrastructure from cyber attacks. Recognized in the Gartner® Magic QuadrantTM for Privileged Access Management (PAM), Keeper combines robust compliance with unmatched visibility and control. With industry-leading certifications, Keeper provides the security assurance public sector organizations require. Learn why agencies trust Keeper to defend against today’s sophisticated adversaries at KeeperSecurity.com.
About The Role
At Keeper, the Inside Sales Account Representatives are responsible for driving new business within an assigned geography or vertical. This is a quota carrying and revenue generating position that reports to our Manager of Inside Sales. This role involves complex selling within a sales cycle period. You will gain a deep understanding of our frontline sales strategies while creating a vision that inspires customers to utilize Keeper as a trusted resource.
Responsibilities
Thrive in a supportive but independent workplace with the opportunity to grow as our organization grows
Target new customers through cold outreach and lead generation campaigns via phone calls and emails
Manage the full sales cycle from initial contact through to closing, ensuring accurate forecasting and reporting
Balance scheduling sales meetings with new clients on a weekly basis
Ensure all customers are on an active Keeper contract
Build and create a constant pipeline of prospect customers to scope
Act as a subject matter expert on all Keeper products, staying knowledgeable and informed of changes, updates, and new products
Participate in cold call/role play activities and shadow cold calls with colleagues
Develop relationships with prospect customer contacts
Utilize additional sales resources to target and identify new business targets
Leverage Salesforce.com database to accurately reflect pipeline and account activity
Facilitate the proposal review process for new business opportunities
Requirements
3+ years of software sales experience
Experience selling identity access management solutions, including PAM (privileged access management)
An accomplished track record of selling software into IT organisations
Salesforce experience
Web-conference demo experience
A track record of exceeding sales quotas
A positive mindset, team-oriented, results driven, and organised
Deadline and detail oriented
Experience managing full sales cycle
Preferred
Bachelor’s degree
Cybersecurity experience
Experience or knowledge of the Information Security industry is highly desired
Excellent problem-solving skills
Proficiency with Microsoft Office & Google Suite programs
Experience working with a Customer Relationship Management tool is preferred, expertise with Salesforce.com is highly desired
Benefits
Onsite lunches
Private healthcare (no wait period)
Pension contribution (no wait period)
Sick Pay
Bike-to-Work Scheme (if local)
Keeper is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Depending on the role and location, the Controller of personal data (the organization responsible for determining why and how personal data is processed) will be Keeper Security Inc. (US), Keeper Security EMEA Ltd. (Ireland), or Keeper Security APAC K.K (Japan).

How We Use Your Data

Legal Basis

jobs.title: Maintenance Technician
jobs.desc:
The Role
We are seeking an experienced Maintenance Technician to join a busy manufacturing environment. The successful candidate will be responsible for supporting preventative and predictive maintenance programmes, carrying out effective maintenance routines and repairs, and ensuring maximum availability and reliability of site equipment.
You will work closely with Operations, Engineering, Process Engineering, Facilities, contractors and equipment suppliers to minimise downtime and support the efficient running of manufacturing operations.
Key Responsibilities
Provide maintenance support to designated manufacturing areas and ensure maximum equipment uptime.
Carry out preventative, predictive and reactive maintenance on a wide range of manufacturing equipment.
Respond quickly and effectively to equipment breakdowns, minimising production downtime.
Diagnose and repair electrical, electronic, pneumatic and hydraulic faults.
Support the Facilities team and liaise with external contractors when required.
Contribute to reliability-centred maintenance programmes and continuous improvement initiatives.
Support the achievement of strong MTTR (Mean Time to Repair) and MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures) performance.
Promote continuous improvement, innovation and lean manufacturing principles.
Support Total Asset Care and 5S programmes across manufacturing and technical areas.
Assist with new product development and new equipment introduction projects.
Maintain accurate records of maintenance activities, including labour hours, spare parts, equipment downtime and repairs, using the site CMMS.
Support the implementation and upkeep of manufacturing equipment excellence programmes.
Ensure all maintenance activities comply with company Health & Safety, Environmental and GMP requirements.
Ensure hazardous and non-hazardous materials are disposed of in accordance with company procedures.
Promote safe and efficient operation of all equipment onsite.
Ensure contractors working within areas of responsibility comply with company safety, environmental and waste management procedures.
Provide timely updates on maintenance activities and work status to relevant maintenance and operations teams.
Adhere to all company procedures and relevant SOPs.
Key Competencies
Strong communication skills.
Highly motivated with a strong work ethic.
Excellent problem-solving and diagnostic ability.
Flexible and adaptable approach to work.
Ability to use initiative and demonstrate innovation.
Strong team player.
Professional, tactful and diplomatic approach.
Continuous improvement mindset.
Essential Qualifications & Experience
Strong electrical and electronic repair and diagnostic skills.
Experience in pneumatic and hydraulic fault finding and repair.
Good understanding of robotics and automated manufacturing systems.
Experience working with high-speed manufacturing equipment.
Experience maintaining and troubleshooting vision systems.
Knowledge of Windows networking.
Some programming experience.
Knowledge of PLCs, drives and HMIs.
Ability to apply strong theoretical knowledge to practical maintenance situations.
Experience working within an FDA-regulated manufacturing environment and understanding of GMP requirements.
Previous experience working in a cleanroom environment.
Strong computer skills.
Third-level qualification in Automation, Mechatronics or a related discipline.
Willingness and ability to travel for a minimum of 3 months for training.
Desirable Experience
Previous experience using a CMMS, preferably Maximo, within a maintenance environment.
3–5 years' experience in an FDA-regulated manufacturing/maintenance environment.
Experience with label printers and label placement equipment.
Experience with FactoryTalk ProductionCentre, Rockwell or SCADA systems.

For over 50 years, we’ve focused on understanding the needs of those working in the public sector, helping our clients access a wide range of financial services—from car, home, health and life insurance to income protection and retirement planning.
We’re proud of the positive impact our work has on individuals, families and communities.

We are currently recruiting Financial Consultants to join our Partnerships Team in Cork, supporting our public sector clients.
In this role, you will work closely with clients to understand their financial needs and goals, helping them make informed decisions about their financial future. You’ll provide tailored advice, identify opportunities to support their wellbeing, and recommend appropriate financial solutions.
This is a fast-paced and collaborative environment, where success is supported through training, coaching and teamwork.
All Financial Consultants receive 8 weeks of comprehensive training
before starting the role. While QFA status (or working towards it) is desirable, we are committed to supporting you—full educational support is provided for those who wish to gain this qualification.

Build trusted relationships with public sector employees and their families
Conduct comprehensive financial wellbeing consultations to understand customers' needs and goals
Provide tailored financial guidance and recommend suitable solutions
Support clients with products such as income protection, life insurance, pensions, retirement planning, and tax services
Deliver presentations and educational sessions within public sector workplaces, including schools and hospitals
Create exceptional customer experiences at every interaction
Respond professionally and efficiently to customer enquiries and referrals
Build long-term customer relationships through specialist advice and ongoing support
Work towards agreed business goals while maintaining a customer-first approach
Maintain the highest standards of compliance and regulatory excellence
Continue developing your financial services knowledge and expertise

As part of a multidisciplinary organisation, you will gain exposure to a broad range of technical challenges while collaborating with experts across engineering, environmental, and planning disciplines.
You will have the chance to take ownership of key hydrological assessments, contribute to high-profile projects, and develop your expertise in flood risk management, drainage, and environmental reporting within the Irish regulatory framework. Being part of a larger international organisation provides access to global best practices, innovative tools, and a wide professional network, while still maintaining a strong local presence and project focus. This is an ideal role for someone looking to advance their career in hydrology, deepen their technical capabilities, and contribute to sustainable water management and climate resilience solutions.
YOUR IMPACT
In this role, you will play a key part in shaping how water is managed across a variety of projects, helping to ensure that development is both sustainable and resilient to future climate challenges. Your work will directly inform critical decisions around flood risk, drainage design, and environmental protection, influencing outcomes for communities, infrastructure, and natural ecosystems.
By delivering robust hydrological assessments and clear, evidence-based insights, you will support clients and project teams in navigating complex regulatory requirements and achieving successful project approvals. Your input will contribute to reducing flood risk, improving water quality, and promoting sustainable development practices across Ireland.
You will also strengthen collaboration within multidisciplinary teams, bringing a hydrology perspective that enhances overall project quality and innovation. Through your technical expertise and proactive approach, you will help drive high standards, build client confidence, and contribute to the continued growth and reputation of the team.

You are a motivated hydrology professional with experience in surface water assessments, data analysis, and environmental reporting within the Irish regulatory context. You have a solid understanding of flood risk management, drainage design principles, and relevant legislation and guidance. With strong analytical, communication, and report-writing skills, you work effectively both independently and as part of multidisciplinary teams. You are enthusiastic about sustainable water management and committed to delivering high-quality technical outputs that support positive environmental outcomes.

Undertaking hydrological assessments including flood risk assessments (FRA), drainage impact assessments, and surface water studies.
Collecting, analysing, and interpreting hydrological and meteorological data.
Supporting the preparation of technical reports and environmental submissions, including EIAR inputs and regulatory assessments.
Contributing to project scoping, planning, and programming activities.
You are adaptable and capable of managing challenging workloads under changing priorities, delivering high-quality results in a dynamic environment.

Growth: We're on an exciting growth journey across the Ireland - we want you to be part of it!
Great Benefits: Competitive salary, enhanced pension plan, annual leave with the option to buy/sell additional days, private medical insurance, group income protection & life assurance included as standard!

Whether you’re starting out on your engineering career or are looking for a fresh challenge, Ryan Hanley, now part of Stantec, is a great career move.

Who are we?
PSC Biotech is a leading Biotech Consultancy firm founded in 1996, headquartered in Pomona, California, USA, with Global operations in Ireland, India, Singapore, Australia and the US, serving 350 clients in more than 23 countries worldwide. We provide cloud-based software solutions for Quality Management and Regulatory Inspections, pharmaceuticals contract manufacturing professionals, and metrology services to our clients.
