Requirements
Role Overview
Operational Excellence 6S Specialist within BcoE. This role is required for 12 months to support lab expansion and we don't have expertise in 6S in the team.
The role would provide dedicated ownership for implementing and sustaining 6S across laboratories areas. Key accountabilities would include programme coordination, workplace assessments, visual standards, audits, action tracking, training, coaching and performance reporting.
The position is proposed as an individual-contributor role . The preferred candidate would have experience in a regulated operational environment, practical 5S or 6S knowledge and strong change-management and facilitation skills.
The role would help strengthen safety, improve workplace organisation and operational flow, and ensure that 6S becomes embedded in daily working practices.
The Operational Excellence 6S Specialist will lead and support the implementation, standardisation and ongoing sustainability of 6S across BCoE laboratories.
6S builds upon the principles of Sort, Set in Order, Shine, Standardise and Sustain, with Safety integrated throughout. The role will help create safe, compliant, efficient and visually managed workplaces that enable colleagues to perform their work effectively and consistently.
This position will partner closely with laboratory teams, scientists, engineers, Environmental Health and Safety,Facilities and BCoE leadership.
The successful candidate will combine practical workplace organisation experience with strong facilitation, coaching, data analysis and change-management skills.
The role supports the organisation’s Operational Excellence expectation that employees actively participate in problem-solving and continuous improvement, while leaders establish improvement goals that make processes more efficient and agile in a compliant manner

We are partnered with a global leader in semiconductors and wireless technology focused on developing high-performance, low-power ASIC solutions for advanced cores and SOCs (System-on-Chips). Perform Static Timing Analysis (STA) and drive timing closure for complex cores and full-chip SOCs (e.g., in the Snapdragon family).

Provide critical feedback to the RTL, Synthesis, and Physical Design teams to improve Power, Performance, and Area (PPA).
Create and execute Timing Engineering Change Orders (ECOs) to resolve critical timing violations.
Enhance techniques and methodologies for timing closure and STA flow accuracy to reduce turnaround time (TAT).
Develop automation scripts (Python, TCL, or Perl) for timing/power data mining and processing.

4+ years of related work experience in Static Timing Analysis.
Expert proficiency in STA tools such as PrimeTime, PrimeShield, or Tempus for hierarchical analysis in large SoCs.
Hands-on experience with ECO tools (e.g., Tweaker, PrimeClosure, PTECO, Tempus ECO) for timing closure.
Highly proficient in automation scripting using Python, TCL, or Perl.
Strong knowledge of the complete ASIC design flow (RTL-to-GDS).

STA Design Engineer / Static Timing Analysis / STA / Timing Closure / ASIC Design / SOC / PrimeTime / Tempus / Timing ECO / PPA Optimization / Gate-Level Netlist / Python / TCL / Physical Design / RTL / Synthesis / Semiconductor / High-Performance Cores

jobs.title: Mechanic - Naval Service: Direct Entry - Engine Room Artificer
jobs.desc:
The Naval Service is the State's principal seagoing agency with a general responsibility to meet contingent and actual maritime defence requirements.
We are now recruiting qualified Maintenance Engineers and Technicians to join as Direct Entry Engine Room Artificers (ERAs). In this role, you'll maintain and repair critical onboard systems including propulsion, power generation and auxiliary machinery. Duties include preventative maintenance, fault diagnosis and participation in emergency response operations at sea.
About the Role:
The Naval Engine Room Artificer (ERA) is responsible for maintaining, repairing and ensuring the efficient operation of ship propulsion systems, power generation and auxiliary machinery
This role requires technical expertise in mechanical and electrical systems, problem-solving skills and the ability to work under pressure in a maritime environment.
ERAs play a vital role in ensuring operational readiness and safety at sea, contributing to the Irish Naval Service’s mission of maritime security and defence.
You will be responsible for conducting planned maintenance and defect rectification on propulsion, electrical and fluid systems.
You will diagnose faults and carry out troubleshooting procedures to ensure continuous operation.
You will assist in emergency response situations, including firefighting and damage control duties.
The role of the ERA works closely with engineering teams to ensure operational efficiency and safety compliance while maintaining accurate records of maintenance, repairs and part replacements.
Eligibility Requirements:
Educational/Professional Qualifications:
HETAC Level 7 in Marine or Mechanical Engineering
QQI Advanced Certificate Craft in:
Mechanical Automation & Maintenance Fitting
Diesel Fitting
Motor Mechanics
Department of Marine & Natural Resources Engineer Officer of the Watch (EOOW) Certificate of Competency
Applicants must be 18 years of age and under 39 years of age: you will be required to provide proof of your age if you progress to the next stage of the competition.
You must be at least 5ft 2in (157.48cm) in height. You will be measured during the selection process.
No tattoos are to be visible above the collar while serving in the Defence Forces. This will be checked during the selection process and you may not proceed if you have visible tattoos above your collar.
Applicants must meet the work permit eligibility criteria to serve as part of the Defence Forces. i.e. You must have a minimum of 5 years eligibility to stay in Ireland. You will be requested to provide proof of working permit on your application.
You must meet medical, physical and security clearance standards, which will be assessed during the recruitment process.
Base Location across: Naval Base, Haulbowline Island, Cork.

jobs.title: Commercial & Operations Associate,
jobs.desc:
Eurofins Scientific
is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.
Job Description
To support the delivery of revenue targets and the organisation's business development and operational activities. The role delivers against defined KPIS to support consistent, profitable and sustainable growth across targeted service lines for the Environment Testing business in Ireland. The Commercial & Operations Associate develops and sustain relationships with new and existing customers and key stakeholders, identifies business development opportunities, and supports the full sales cycle from lead generation, tendering and contract award through to operational handover and service delivery. The role also provides account management for newly won work and a selected portfolio of existing customers, while assisting with the planning and scheduling of driver jobs in synchro teams.
REPORTING TO Commercial & Operations Manager
Main Commercial responsibilities Will include:
Identify leads and develop prospects to generate a project pipeline of sufficient value to achieve and sustain growth  objectives.
Maintain pipeline updates and records on a weekly basis and assist with preparation of weekly commercial reports.
Manage a selected portfolio of existing customer accounts, maintaining regular contact, supporting issue resolution and identifying opportunities to improve service delivery and develop the account.
Work with Group Marketing to develop materials and tools that support business development and promote the Eurofins brand.
Resolve or escalate commercial issues and negotiations, with support from functional leads where required.
Support tender processes by conducting quality reviews to understand logistics, operational and technical requirements, incorporating feedback from functional leads and developing high-quality proposals that meet the required service and quality standards.
Conduct market research and competitor analysis.
Manage Customer queries, complaints and escalation processes.
Main Operations responsibilities Will include:
Assist with the Planning and scheduling of jobs in Synchro teams for drivers, ensuring that available job information and customer requirements are accurately reflected to Support efficient service delivery.
Review scheduled routes to target new customers on selected routes.
Monitor customer satisfaction and service delivery for existing clients though monthly NPS.
Own the account management and mobilisation of newly won work from contract award through to stable operational delivery, acting as a clear point of contact for the customer and internal stakeholders.
Work with laboratory, logistics and operations teams to drive service improvements.
Ensure customer sampling requirements are translated into operational plans.
Assist with contingency planning for resource shortages, holidays and peak workloads.
Qualifications
EDUCATION / EXPERIENCE
What we are looking for:
Previous experience working within an accredited contract testing laboratory or related industry laboratory environment preferred.
Previous customer facing experience preferred.
Who we are looking for:
Hard-working, self-motivated and professional team player.
Confident and effective communicator and relationship builder.
Ability to work well under pressure.
Excellent attention to detail.
Ability to multitask, prioritise, organise and co-ordinate your own workload.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Microsoft office experience is an advantage
Additional Information
What can we offer you?
Fixed term contract;
Flexible working hours;
A dynamic team with flat hierarchies and opportunities for active participation;
Personal and professional development opportunities, as well as exclusive benefits for Eurofins employees;
We support your development!
Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.
We embrace diversity!
Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an
Equal Opportunity Employer
. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.
Sustainability matters to us!
We are well on our way to achieving our objective of carbon neutrality by 2025, through a combination of emission reduction and compensation initiatives. We encourage our laboratory leaders to make sustainable changes at their local level, and in addition to their initiatives we also count on our dedicated carbon reduction team to help us to achieve this goal!
Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/
Company description:
Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic and labelling is accurate.
The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and agroscience contract research services. It is one of the market leaders in certain testing and laboratory services for genomics, discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and in the support of clinical studies, as well as having an emerging global presence in Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisations. It also has a rapidly developing presence in highly specialised and molecular clinical diagnostic testing and in-vitro diagnostic products.
In over 35 years, Eurofins has grown from one laboratory in Nantes, France to ca. 65,000 staff across a decentralised and entrepreneurial network of 950 laboratories in 60 countries. Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products.
In 2024, Eurofins generated total revenues of EUR 6.9 billion, and has been among the best performing stocks in Europe over the past 20 years.

jobs.title: Calibration Technician
jobs.desc:
LotusWorks is an Engineering Services provider specializing in managing Commissioning, Construction Services, Calibration, Operations & Maintenance scopes of work within global manufacturing facilities. LotusWorks operates globally across EMEA and North America partnering with the world's leading manufacturers across the Semiconductor, Pharmaceutical & Biologics, Medical Device and Data Center sectors. Our team of Engineering and Technical professionals is immersed in cutting-edge technologies and innovations. LotusWorks is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace, integral to our people-first approach.
As a Calibration Technician, you will report directly to the Site Lead and carry out planned and unplanned calibration activities in line with the calibration schedule prepared by the Lead Calibration Technician. The role will have a strong focus on process calibrations, while also supporting gauging calibrations as required. You will ensure that all Inspection, Measurement and Test Equipment (IMTE) is calibrated safely, on time, and in accordance with site quality requirements, with accurate completion of calibration records and timely escalation of any calibration issues. Safety is a line responsibility, and all personnel are responsible for ensuring that work is conducted safely within their direct or indirect supervision.
Responsibilities
Operations & Maintenance
Complete assigned calibration activities in accordance with the schedule prepared by the Lead Calibration Technician, escalating any risks to completion or equipment availability.
Perform process calibrations including pressure transmitters, transducers, manometers, ovens, furnaces, temperature controllers, freezers, pH and conductivity equipment, cleanrooms, cleanlines, refractometers, ultrasonic baths, packaging equipment and other process instrumentation.
Support gauging calibrations, including calipers, micrometers, pin, plug and thread gauges, drop gauges, overlay and TAPPI charts, CMM calibrations and air gauging systems.
Execute planned and reactive calibration activities in a safe, timely and compliant manner, minimizing disruption to production.
Promptly escalate calibration failures, technical issues and any risks to equipment availability.
Quality
Ensure calibration work orders, as-found/as-left results and associated records are completed accurately and on time within the calibration system and in accordance with site standards.
Follow approved procedures and Equipment Work Instructions (EWIs).
Escalate out-of-tolerance or failed calibrations in accordance with site procedures.
Support discrepancy investigations and ensure required actions are completed.
Complete all required training and maintain audit-ready calibration documentation.
Governance & Relationship Management
Report directly to the Site Lead and work to the operational priorities established through the Lead Calibration Technician.
Escalate schedule, quality, safety and technical issues as required.
Maintain strong working relationships with onsite equipment owners and users to coordinate calibration activities and ensure equipment readiness and access.
Collaborate with Quality, EHS, Engineering, Maintenance, Production and Metrology teams to support compliant calibration execution and troubleshooting.
Provide clear and timely updates on calibration progress, equipment failures, delays and required actions.
Resource Management
Manage assigned daily calibration activities efficiently and complete work within agreed priorities and due dates.
Support other Calibration Technicians and participate in cross-training to improve flexibility and coverage across process and gauging activities.
Maintain and develop technical competence in process instrumentation, calibration standards, troubleshooting and site calibration procedures.
Support Functions
Support the creation, review and continuous improvement of Equipment Work Instructions (EWIs), calibration procedures, Calibration Record Forms (CRFs) and Calibration Data Forms (CDFs), where required.
Adhere to all site Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS) requirements and the Life Without (LW) safety culture during all calibration activities.
Identify and support opportunities to improve calibration methods, workflow, equipment reliability, efficiency and compliance.
Any other duties or responsibilities that may be assigned to you in your role.
Skills Required
Practical experience in calibration, metrology, instrumentation or a related technical discipline.
Strong knowledge of process instrumentation and calibration principles.
Experience calibrating pressure, temperature, pH, conductivity and other process instrumentation.
Experience with gauging equipment and dimensional measurement techniques is desirable.
Ability to interpret technical procedures, Equipment Work Instructions (EWIs) and calibration documentation.
Strong attention to detail and a commitment to accurate documentation and data integrity.
Ability to identify, troubleshoot and escalate calibration failures and out-of-tolerance conditions.
Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple calibration activities and priorities.
Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work collaboratively with equipment owners and cross-functional teams.
Commitment to maintaining high standards of quality, safety and compliance.
Willingness to participate in cross-training and continued technical development.
Education / Licenses / Certifications
Minimum of Level 7 Qualification in Calibration/Engineering/Metrology or Process Instrumentation.
Proof of education, licenses, and certifications will be required where applicable

VHI Healthcare Cover
Life Assurance
Pension Contribution
Training And Educational Assistance
Annual GP Check-Up
Extra Annual Leave
Healthcare Screening
Recognition Rewards

jobs.title: Pre-Sales Solutions Architect – AI Agent & Workload Security
jobs.desc:
Tigera—the pioneer behind Calico and Lynx—is defining the future of AI agent security, workload governance, and cloud-native networking. As autonomous AI agents, LLM frameworks, and microservices proliferate across enterprise infrastructure, Tigera delivers the deep visibility, runtime protection, and eBPF-driven enforcement control required to secure the next generation of computing.
From modern cloud-native architectures to cutting-edge AI agent ecosystems, our technology safeguards over 1 million Kubernetes clusters across multicloud and hybrid environments. Trusted by world-class innovation leaders—including NVIDIA, Royal Bank of Canada, Bloomberg, Chipotle, GoDaddy, and Upwork—we empower enterprises to build, scale, and innovate with AI safely and without compromise.
At Tigera, our customers are the heroes of our story. We aim high, move fast, foster continuous learning, and build a high-trust, highly collaborative environment where every voice shapes the future of AI security. If you are looking to help make a substantial impact, and our values and products align with your vision of your career growth, we want to hear from you!
The Opportunity
AI agents are rapidly becoming the new runtime layer of the enterprise—and securing them is the next massive frontier in cybersecurity.
We are hiring a
Pre-Sales Solutions Architect
in
Cork, Ireland
, to serve as the technical champion for
Lynx
, our flagship solution designed specifically to secure autonomous AI agents and modern workloads. With customer demand skyrocketing and PoCs accelerating globally, you will be on the front lines of a brand-new product category.
You will partner closely with Account Executives, Product Management, and Marketing to guide prospective enterprises from initial architecture discussions through high-impact PoCs to closed-won deals. Additionally, you will work with our enterprise Calico accounts to unlock additional value by securing AI workloads.
This role is ideal for a forward-thinking pre-sales professional or platform/security engineer eager to spearhead AI agent security while the category is being defined. You don’t need to be an AI expert on day one—if you bring strong Kubernetes and application security foundations along with a passion for how AI systems are built, we will help you build the required expertise.
The role will be hybrid based out of our Cork city office.
You Will
Drive AI & Workload Security Deals: Lead the technical discovery, live demonstrations, solution architecture, and proof-of-concept (PoC) executions for Lynx across top-tier enterprise prospects.
Shape AI Security Requirements: Partner directly with prospects to discover how they build, deploy, and connect AI agents, and help them convert runtime patterns into concrete security and governance policies using Lynx.
Build Reusable Assets: Design and maintain state-of-the-art Lynx demo environments, PoC playbooks, and architecture blueprints to increase deal velocity.
Influence the Product Roadmap: Serve as the strategic feedback loop between the field and product engineering. Capture customer requirements, highlight market shifts, and directly influence the evolution of Lynx.
Champion the AI Security Movement: Represent Tigera as an author and speaker. Deliver technical webinars, lead workshops, participate in meetups/conferences, and publish insights on securing AI agents.
Master Technical Execution: Lead technical RFP/RFI responses, security questionnaire validations, and internal enablement sessions on AI agent security.
Guide Strategic Enterprise Accounts: Act as the trusted technical advisor for a dedicated set of Calico accounts. Drive platform adoption, conduct technical architecture reviews, and uncover expansion opportunities into Lynx.
Travel: Connect in person with enterprise clients and attend industry events across Europe (approx. 25% travel).
You Have
Pre-Sales or Hands-On Engineering Experience: 3 to 6 years in a customer-facing technical role (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Technical Consultant) OR hands-on experience in platform, DevOps, or cloud security engineering with a driven desire to launch a career in pre-sales.
Core Cloud-Native Foundations: Strong, hands-on experience with Kubernetes and containerized architectures. You can comfortably stand up clusters, troubleshoot complex workloads, and explain core container runtime mechanics.
Security Discipline: Deep understanding of modern application and cloud security principles, including Zero Trust models, network policies, identity-based security, and cloud access controls.
Identity & Token Knowledge: Practical understanding of identity-first security—how JWTs are structured, signed, and validated; working knowledge of OAuth 2.0, OIDC, and mTLS mechanics.
Cloud Infrastructure: Hands-on experience with at least one major cloud platform (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
Sales Acumen: Sales skills such as active listening, MEDDPICC alignment and ability to translate features into business value.
Exceptional Communication: Natural ability to translate complex AI runtime mechanics and Zero Trust architectures into clear, compelling narratives for both hands-on engineers and C-level executives.
Startup Mindset: Curious, self-driven, and excited by the opportunity to own and establish leadership in an emerging category.
Nice to Have (Bonus Points)
Hands-on exposure to building or securing AI/LLM applications or agents (e.g., LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, or Model Context Protocol / MCP servers).
Familiarity with workload identity frameworks (e.g., SPIFFE/SPIRE) or API gateways / service meshes (Istio, Envoy).
Prior experience with Calico, Cilium, OpenShift, or eBPF technology.
Familiarity with emerging AI governance frameworks (EU AI Act, ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF).
Proficiency in a second European language.
Why Join Tigera?
Be at the Forefront of AI: Build your career at the intersection of eBPF, Kubernetes, and AI agent security.
Global Impact, Local Hub: Join a vibrant hub in Cork, Ireland, backed by global offices in San Francisco, San Jose, Vancouver, and London.
Comprehensive Compensation & Benefits: Highly competitive salary, sales incentive plans, and comprehensive health, vision, and dental coverage.
Culture of Growth & Autonomy: Work alongside industry experts who value openness, continuous learning, bold execution, and genuine team support.
With offices in San Francisco, San Jose, Vancouver (Canada), Cork (Ireland), and London (England), we have a thriving team of diverse individuals from all over the world. We believe in a collaborative, flexible work environment based on respect for, and commitment from, every employee. We also offer a competitive compensation package along with full health, vision, and dental benefits. These benefits, coupled with an amazing team of individuals who believe in our mission and value openness, collaboration, and teamwork, make Tigera an awesome place to work.

jobs.title: Applied AI Technology Specialist
jobs.desc:
Company Overview
Carbery Group is dedicated to enriching lives. How do we do this? Owned by the farmers of West Cork, we are a global business with deep local roots. Our mission is to deliver lasting value to our farmer shareholders while making positive impact on our customers, employees, suppliers, partners, and the communities we serve. We are committed to doing this by creating healthier, tastier, and more sustainable food and ingredient solutions.
With customers in over 50 countries, we pride ourselves on our commitment to innovation, our open mindset and ability to be a good partner. We prioritise our customers' needs, while also valuing our planet and fostering a thriving, people-first environment.
Your Role in Carbery's Success
As an Applied AI Technology Specialist, you will work closely with the group CIO to ensure that Carbery genuinely keeps current with how AI is evolving. You will bring deep, current knowledge of the AI landscape and test what is genuinely worth pursuing, while working alongside the senior team to help bring proven ideas into the business.
How You Will Contribute
Continuously track emerging AI models, tools, research and practitioner practice, and translate that into a short, opinionated shortlist of what's genuinely relevant to Carbery.
Build and run small, hands-on prototypes against genuine internal business problems, reaching a clear keep-or-kill verdict on each.
Say no, clearly and in writing, to AI trends that are hype-driven or don't fit Carbery's data and regulatory reality — as often as flagging things worth pursuing.
Own the transition of proven concepts from pilot to full production scale, in partnership with the Digital team and whoever will operate the solution day to day.
Present evidence-based updates at agreed Group Leadership Team sessions, scoped to what has actually been tested and what's being scaled
Manage a budget for licences, prototyping tools and short-term experimentation.
Build the business case for scaling proven pilots into production, jointly with the Group CIO.
Essential Requirements
Meaningful experience (4+ years) in an AI, data, software or automation role, with direct hands-on build experience, not only strategy or advisory exposure.
A demonstrable habit of following AI developments closely — able to speak specifically to what's changed recently
Strong working knowledge of the LLM/SLM landscape, plus awareness of domain-specific and open-source alternatives.
Practical experience building and testing prototypes, proofs of concept or small tools in a real business setting, and taking at least one through to production or live use.
Genuinely immersed in the evolving AI landscape; new models, tools and techniques and able to separate what's real from what's well-marketed.
Clear, confident communication skills, able to present tested findings to senior stakeholders and contribute to strategic direction alongside a more senior sponsor.
Desirable Requirements
A degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering or a related field.
Exposure to manufacturing or FMCG environments.
Our Commitment to our People
We are a diverse and growing workforce of over 1,000 people across eight countries globally. As we continue to grow, we want to ensure that Carbery Group continues to be a place where people are supported to develop and feel that they can do their best work. We are committed to driving growth, developing future capability and delivering results through our dedicated teams.
We offer competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and an inclusive workplace where your skills, perspectives, and experience help shape the future of our industry. Join us and be part of a team that values collaboration and makes a meaningful impact - from local communities to global markets.
Carbery Group is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to fostering a supportive work environment.

jobs.desc:
About the role
We pride ourselves on offering customers the biggest range of products around. And that's not just food, but everything from clothes and kettles to financial services.
But did you know we offer the biggest job opportunities too? With stores across the UK and Ireland, and a variety of roles, we are always looking for people who are as passionate about helping customers as we are.
Our Every Little Helps approach doesn't just apply to our customers. It's at the very heart of everything we do at work - and it's what makes us different. We believe in treating each other with respect, and everyone having the opportunity to get on. That's what makes Tesco such a great place to work.

Always put the customer first and consider them in everything you do.
Get to know your customers and serve them with pride.

Follow all company policies and adhere to Health and Safety routines.

You will need
Able to give great, natural customer service by proactively smiling, greeting, acknowledging and helping customers.
Works hard for customers, your team and your department.
You are able to prioritise to ensure anything you do is right for our customers.
Adaptable and resilient to meet the ever changing demands of our business.
You must be able to follow instructions either verbal or written.
You are reliable and a good timekeeper.
You must be smart and tidy at all times.
Whats in it for you?
We offer excellent benefits that help make Tesco a great place to work. These include but aren't limited to:
Competitive Salary
Bonus Scheme*
Our Virtual GP service provides free and confidential access to an online GP through video GP consultations, and online prescription service for colleagues. The service is also available to families of colleagues who live at the same address for a reduced cost.
24/7 access to our Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) for you and family members for in the moment emotional support along with free access to a range of wellbeing services supporting you under our new Wellbeing First approach of Body, Mind and Life.
Colleague Clubcard offering 10% discount across stores and online, with 15% discount weekends once a month (Friday to Sunday), and 20% off twice a year. There is also 20% off F&F clothing, all year long, these various discounts can be extended to a family member with a 2nd Clubcard available.*
Life Assurance
Pension Plan*
Save As You Earn Scheme*
Paid Family Leave
Bike to Work
Long Service Awards
Commuter Scheme

About Us
Our vision at Tesco is to become every customer's favourite way to shop, whether they are at home or out on the move. Our core purpose is "Serving our customers, communities and planet a little better every day". Serving means more than a transactional relationship with our customers. It means acting as a responsible and sustainable business for all stakeholders, for the communities we are part of, and for the planet. Through initiatives like the Tesco Community Fund, our association with Children's Health Foundation, our partnership with FoodCloud and our Stronger Starts programme, we have supported over 21,000 community groups, raised over €7.5 million for medical equipment, and provided almost 15 million meals nationwide, to those living in food insecurity.
Tesco has operated in the Irish retail market since 1997, and with 190+ stores nationwide, we employ over 13,000 people in cities and towns around Ireland, supporting almost 45,000 jobs directly and indirectly. We partner with over 500 Irish suppliers - of which almost three-quarters are small and medium enterprises - which in turn supports almost 13,000 farming families around Ireland. Tesco is the single largest buyer of Irish food and drink in the world, buying €1.6 Billion a year; more than any other single country in the European Union, more than even the USA which you perceive as a massive buyer of Irish food.
We work closely with suppliers across Ireland who are dedicated to making the best products for our customers and this is reflected in the numerous awards our products have won over the years including Blás Na hÉireann, World Steak Challenge and Great Taste Awards.
We are proud to have an inclusive culture at Tesco where everyone truly feels able to be themselves. It is embedded in our values: we treat people how they want to be treated. At Tesco, we not only celebrate diversity, but recognise the value and opportunity it brings. We always want our colleagues to feel they can be themselves at work and we are committed to helping them be at their best.
We know life looks a little different for each of us. That's why at Tesco, we always welcome chats about flexible working. Some people are at the start of their careers, some want the freedom to do the things they love. Others are going through life-changing moments like becoming a carer, nearing retirement, adapting to parenthood, or something else. So, talk to us throughout your application about how we can support.
Tesco is committed to celebrating diversity and everyone is welcome at Tesco. We're committed to providing a fully inclusive recruitment process, allowing candidates the opportunity to thrive and inform us of any reasonable adjustments they may require. For further information on the accessibility support we can offer, please click http://roi.tesco-careers.com/accessibility/

Please let us know you need additional support by emailing tescoireland.recruitment@tesco.ie
This will allow us to understand more about you and how we can best support you through the recruitment process.
